entities.summary:
Electronic Arts (EA), founded in 1982 by Trip Hawkins in Redwood City, California, has emerged as a cornerstone of the video game industry, significantly influencing both gaming culture and technology. Initially focused on publishing computer games, EA grew into a global powerhouse, with franchises such as "Madden NFL," "The Sims," and "FIFA" that have collectively sold hundreds of millions of copies worldwide. This institution has not only shaped entertainment practices but also transformed the economic landscape of the digital age, establishing new business models and marketing strategies that have been widely adopted across the sector.

Throughout the years, EA made notable strides in game development and publishing, pioneering advancements in graphics and gameplay mechanics that set new industry standards. The introduction of online multiplayer features in the late 1990s revolutionized how players interacted, culminating in the creation of EA Sports, which became synonymous with sports gaming. EA's acquisition of smaller studios and franchises, such as BioWare and Respawn Entertainment, further diversified its portfolio, showcasing a commitment to innovation and quality storytelling in video games.

The legacy of Electronic Arts extends beyond its commercial success, as it has played a crucial role in the rise of eSports and competitive gaming. By organizing tournaments and sponsoring teams, EA has helped elevate gaming to a spectator sport, attracting millions of viewers and participants globally. This cultural shift has not only transformed perceptions of gaming but has also influenced how media and advertisements are tailored to engage younger audiences, marking a significant evolution in entertainment.
